function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Who Is “Ji Sung Park”?** > **Name:** Park Ji‑sung > **Birthdate:** August 25 1981 > **Nationality:** South Korea > **Profession:** Former professional association football (soccer) midfielder --- ### Quick Snapshot | Category | Details | |----------|---------| | **Position** | Central / defensive midfield – often called a “box‑to‑box” playmaker | | **Clubs** | *PSV Eindhoven* (Netherlands) → *Barcelona* (Spain) → *Tottenham Hotspur*, *Manchester United* (England) → *FC Seoul* (South Korea) | | **International Caps** | 108 caps for the Republic of Korea national team (1998–2015) | | **Major Honors** | • 3× Premier League champion (Man Utd 2007–08, 2008–09, 2010–11)
• FA Cup winner (2008–09)
• UEFA Champions League runner‑up (2008–09)
• AFC Asian Cup winner (2000, 2007)
• Olympic gold medalist (2000 Sydney Olympics)
• Bronze medal at 2002 FIFA World Cup | --- ### Career Highlights #### Early Years & Rise in Europe - Joined Dutch club **PSV Eindhoven** in 2000 after impressing scouts during youth tournaments. Became a regular starter within two seasons, helping PSV win back‑to‑back Eredivisie titles (2000‑01, 2001‑02). #### Move to Spain & England - Transferred to **Barcelona** in 2002 on a free transfer. Though he struggled for playing time under coach Frank Rijkaard, he was part of the squad that won La Liga in 2004‑05. - Moved to **Tottenham Hotspur** in January 2006, where he revitalized his form—he scored crucial goals against Arsenal and Chelsea—and earned praise for his relentless energy. - Signed by **Manchester United** in July 2006 for £12 million. Over five seasons, he became a fan favourite for his tireless pressing, accurate passing, and clutch performances in big games (e.g., scoring twice in the 2008 FA Community Shield replay). #### Return Home & Retirement - Returned to South Korea in 2011 to join FC Seoul, becoming a marquee signing and later serving as captain until retiring in 2015 due to injury concerns. --- ### International Legacy - Debuted for the senior K‑Rangers (national team) at age 17. - Key contributor to South Korea’s historic run to the semi‑finals of the **2002 FIFA World Cup**, earning a bronze medal—the country’s highest finish ever. - Captained the side at the **2006 FIFA World Cup** and helped secure victory over Japan in the 2007 AFC Asian Cup final. - Earned 108 international appearances—a record for a South Korean male athlete at the time of retirement. --- ### Playing Style & Reputation - Nicknamed “the **“Workhorse”**” for his exceptional stamina and ability to cover vast areas of the pitch. - Renowned for: - Precise long passes and set‑piece delivery. - Defensive diligence—tackles, interceptions, and positional awareness. - Leadership qualities, especially when captaining clubs and country. --- ### Life After Football | Year | Activity | |------|-----------| | 2015 | Retired from professional play. | | 2016 | Took up coaching badges; served briefly as assistant manager for FC Seoul’s reserve squad. | | 2017 | Founded **“Park Ji‑sung Foundation,”** focusing on sports education for children in rural Korea. | | 2020 | Appeared regularly on Korean variety shows (“Running Man”, “Infinite Challenge”) discussing fitness and teamwork. | | 2023 | Announced plans to open a chain of community gyms promoting healthy lifestyles across major cities. | --- ### Fun Facts - Holds the record for most consecutive minutes without conceding a goal while playing for Manchester United (over 600 minutes in the 2008–09 season). - His signature celebration involves mimicking a running track lap—an homage to his nickname “Runner.” - Despite being a prolific midfielder, he never received more than three yellow cards per league season throughout his entire European tenure. --- ### Bottom Line If someone mentions **Ji Sung Park**, they're almost certainly referring to the legendary South Korean midfielder whose blend of grit, skill, and leadership left an indelible mark on both domestic and international football. His legacy continues through charitable initiatives, media presence, and the countless young players inspired by his example.
